A_target.statement:
Let $t_n$ be the number of [[Definition:Binary Tree|binary trees]] with $n$ internal nodes, and $\map T x = \displaystyle \sum_{n \mathop \ge 0} t_n x^n$.
Then $\map T x$ is the [[Definition:Unique|unique]] [[Definition:Formal Power Series|formal power series]] with constant term $1$ satisfying:
:$\map T x = 1 + x \map T x^2$

B_source.statement:
Let a functional equation $F = \map \Phi F$ on [[Definition:Formal Power Series|formal power series]] determine the coefficient of $x^n$ in $\map \Phi F$ from the coefficients of $F$ below $n$.
Then the equation has a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] solution.

substitutions.the operator on formal power series: the map sending a series F to 1 + x F squared
substitutions.the fixed point of the operator: the generating function for binary trees
substitutions.the determination of coefficients from e: the recursive decomposition of a tree into its two subtrees

derived.the fixed point equation: the functional equation for the generating function
derived.iteration converging coefficientwise: each coefficient stabilizes after finitely many iterations

object_map.reformulation: Read the recursive structure of the objects as a fixed point equation on their generating function.

validity_conditions: The factor of x shifts degrees, so the coefficient of x to the n in the image depends only on coefficients below n; this is what makes the operator determine a unique fixed point.
Convergence is formal rather than analytic: each coefficient stabilizes after finitely many iterations, so no analytic convergence is needed.
The functional equation encodes the recursive decomposition of a nonempty binary tree into a root and two subtrees, which is why the square appears.
proof_plan: A binary tree is either a leaf, or a root together with an ordered pair of subtrees.

Translating into [[Definition:Generating Function|generating functions]], with $x$ marking the root:
:$\map T x = 1 + x \map T x^2$
Regard this as $T = \map \Phi T$ with $\map \Phi F = 1 + x F^2$.
